findings.reason: the "removed-pointer case classifies with no session_refusal" assertion stays red for a reason the plan never names, so a worker implementing this literally would either report a spurious defect or "fix" it by editing the refusal text instead of the class branch, which is the one place that must return None.
findings.text: §2 says that when no named run has a live pointer the remedy "returns no remedy, which is the waiting reading", but `_queued_failure_remedy` (`reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:255-258`) only `return`s on a non-None helper result; on None it falls through to `_remedy_command_stated_by(text)` (:286), and the recorded D11 text quotes the command `reckon crew dispatch --allow-unreconciled-runs` in `refusals.py:47-50`, so the published next command is a re-dispatch — reproduced: with the helper patched to return None, `_queued_failure_remedy` returns `next_command: reckon crew dispatch --allow-unreconciled-runs`.

findings.reason: the actionable field is `next_command`, which §2 does redirect to the live run's own reconcile action; the detail is advice a coordinator can weigh, so it does not send the node down a different implementation path.
findings.text: the retained remedy detail still ends "the alternative is to discard the queued run and dispatch again with --allow-unreconciled-runs" (`recovery_classification.py:194-201`), which is the action §1 states a queued run must never be told to take because it "discards the request's place"; the plan's deliverable leaves that sentence in place.
